claim.pdf_says: 13.15.2 General format, the USAGE line is printed inside its OWN OUTER BRACKET spanning both rows:  ⎡ [ USAGE IS ] ⎧ DISPLAY ⎫ ⎤ / ⎣               ⎩ NATIONAL ⎭ ⎦ . Verified at 300 dpi: a square bracket opens to the left of the inner '[ USAGE IS ]' and closes to the right of the brace's '}'. USAGE, DISPLAY and NATIONAL are underlined; IS is not.
claim.why_it_matters: The outer bracket is what makes the whole USAGE clause optional in a report group description entry. Stripped of it, the markdown reads as a mandatory brace: every report-group entry would be required to state DISPLAY or NATIONAL. That is falsely restrictive — the clause is optional, which is also what 13.15.4 general rule 2) presupposes when it says the USAGE clause, when present, behaves as in a data description entry. Every other clause on this page is shown bracketed/optional; USAGE is the only one whose bracket was dropped.

verdict.reasoning:
CONFIRMED by direct inspection of the 300 dpi render (E:/Temp/specrecon/v389/spec_p389.png, cropped and 3x upscaled to usage_zoom.png). Reading the printed glyphs left to right on the USAGE row of 13.15.2, I see: (1) a TALL SQUARE BRACKET '[' whose vertical stroke spans both the DISPLAY row and the NATIONAL row, with the characteristic top and bottom horizontal serifs; (2) a short, single-row-height '[ USAGE IS ]' with USAGE underlined and IS NOT underlined; (3) a tall BRACE '{' spanning both rows; (4) DISPLAY (underlined) stacked over NATIONAL (underlined); (5) a tall closing BRACE '}'; (6) a TALL SQUARE BRACKET ']' with top and bottom serifs, closing the pair opened in (1). So the outer delimiter is a CLOSED square-bracket pair enclosing the entire clause, brace and all — exactly as claimed. The claim's description of the underlining is also exactly right.

The outer bracket is not a stacking/'cases' artifact. On the same page the source-clause/sum-clause/value-clause stack is delimited by a closed square-bracket pair (optional choice) and PRESENT WHEN condition-1 by a closed square-bracket pair, while the DISPLAY/NATIONAL choice uses BRACES — i.e. this page distinguishes brackets from braces exactly per the ISO metalanguage, and the USAGE row carries both, nested.

The markdown genuinely lacks it. specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 16688-16707 (the 13.15.2 fenced block, identical to the extracted page-389.md lines 17-36) render the row as '  [ USAGE IS ] { DISPLAY  }' / '               { NATIONAL }' with no outer bracket. Under the metalanguage that is a REQUIRED choice, so the transcription makes a USAGE clause naming DISPLAY or NATIONAL mandatory in every report group description entry — falsely restrictive, and it would make a compiler built from the markdown reject legal COBOL.

Not a convention or formatting artifact: the same transcription preserves this exact nested shape elsewhere. specs/ISO_COBOL.md 13.16.2 Format 1 writes '[ [ SIGN IS ] { LEADING  } [ SEPARATE CHARACTER ] ]' / '{ TRAILING }' and '[ GROUP-USAGE IS { BIT      } ]' / '{ NATIONAL }' — outer optional bracket retained around an inner brace choice. Page 389 is a one-off drop, not a house style.

Corroboration that optional is the correct reading: nothing in 13.15.3 syntax rules 1)-17) requires a USAGE clause (contrast SR 5, which explicitly requires TYPE in every level 1 entry even though type-clause is bracketed — showing the bracket carries optionality and the syntax rules add the obligations), and 13.15.4 GR 2 groups USAGE with PICTURE, BLANK WHEN ZERO and JUSTIFIED, all three of which are bracketed on this page, deferring their rules to the data description entry where usage-clause is likewise optional.
verdict.corrected_description:
Accurate as filed; no correction needed. Refinements for the fix: the dropped delimiter is a closed tall square-bracket PAIR spanning both stacked rows and enclosing the inner '[ USAGE IS ]' plus the whole '{ DISPLAY / NATIONAL }' brace. Restore it using the transcription's own established convention (cf. 13.16.2 Format 1 '[ [ SIGN IS ] { LEADING } [ SEPARATE CHARACTER ] ]' and '[ GROUP-USAGE IS { BIT } ]'), i.e.:
  [ [ USAGE IS ] { DISPLAY  } ]
                 { NATIONAL }
One detail of the claim's rationale is slightly overstated but immaterial: 13.15.4 GR 2 does not itself say 'when present'; it says the USAGE, PICTURE, BLANK WHEN ZERO and JUSTIFIED clauses are the same clauses as in a data description entry and obey those clauses' rules — which implies optionality only by grouping USAGE with three clauses that are printed bracketed here and by the absence of any syntax rule mandating USAGE. The load-bearing evidence is the printed outer bracket itself, which is unambiguous.
